solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cry from one trapped in factory

indicators.note: something trapped in a place sits inside it, so one goes within the factory word

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A worker stuck inside an industrial works calls out for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaint is a lament or complaint, an expression of grief, which is a kind of cry.

clue.text: A sticky end for pilot with cargo of soft food

indicators.note: carrying a cargo means holding something inside, so the pilot word contains the food word

parts.note: a pilot is a flyer, one who flies aircraft
pap is bland, soft food for infants or invalids

explanation.surface: An aviator meets a messy demise while carrying a load of mushy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sticky end' usually means a nasty death; here it is literal, a sticky strip that ends the life of flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is a strip coated in adhesive on which insects die, literally a sticky end for them.

clue.text: Part of Oxford society?

parts.note: an Oxford is also a style of shoe, whose top section is called the upper, while the rest of the phrase points to the social stratum of privilege often linked with Oxford University

explanation.surface: A question about which social group populates the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a laced leather shoe; the leather covering the top of a shoe is its upper.
explanation.definitionFit: The privileged social stratum is the upper class, and an Oxford shoe has an upper part too.

clue.text: Flog defender after footballer's first scene in film

indicators.note: the flog and defender words come after the footballer's initial
the first of a word is its opening letter, here of the footballer's

parts.note: to flog is to lash or whip
a back is a defending player in football

explanation.surface: A command to whip a defensive player who comes behind a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashback is a scene in a film that cuts back to earlier events.

clue.text: Crawl from the Devon and Cornwall motorway northwards

parts.note: Devon and Cornwall are the English counties of the South West, abbreviated SW

indicators.note: in a down entry, going northwards means reading upwards, so the motorway letters are reversed

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Traffic crawls up the motorway out of England's south-western peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawl' looks like slow traffic, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is a swimming stroke, so to crawl is to swim using it.

clue.text: Hear of hurry, getting first-class return from the country

indicators.note: asks for the word for hurry as it would be heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: to hurry is to rush

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry for a first-class journey home from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a country, the largest by area in the world.

clue.text: The way to encourage fish

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Advice on how best to coax a fish along.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, sold as caviar.

clue.text: Where to see a frog play around, wearing cap?

indicators.note: the anagram wears the cap, so the cap word goes round it

parts.note: a lid is a cap or cover

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of play are moved about

explanation.surface: Asks where a frog might be found fooling about in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals LYPA, the anagram of PLAY, which goes inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs are commonly pictured sitting on the floating leaves of water lilies.

clue.text: Bowl a stunner?

definitions.meaning: a bowl is a deep serving vessel, a container for food
an attractive person is informally called this

explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a bowl-like vessel, and slang calls a very attractive person a dish.

clue.text: Dress for action?

parts.note: an outfit, a set of matching clothes, for a legal action in court

explanation.surface: Advice to get changed before going into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: An action is a legal proceeding; a suit is an outfit, so the phrase reads as courtroom clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal action brought in court, and suit also means a set of clothes.

clue.text: Invokes admiration, rejecting house full of journalists

indicators.note: the house is filled, so the journalists word goes inside it
rejecting turns something back, so the house letters run backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, very common in Britain
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Something wins praise by turning away a home crowded with reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns SEMI into IMES, which holds PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress someone is to draw their admiration; the clue's 'invokes' stands loosely for evokes.

clue.text: Scrooge is a gentleman with no time

indicators.note: having no time means that letter is taken away

parts.note: a gentleman is addressed as mister

explanation.surface: A remark that Scrooge is a gentleman who can never spare a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, from Dickens, is the archetypal skinflint who hoards money.

clue.text: Subject to snap

parts.note: a snap is a photograph, informally a pic

explanation.surface: Something liable to break suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a discussion or piece of writing.

clue.text: Perhaps the Stones grow old and get medical cover

parts.note: the Rolling Stones are an example of a rock band
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: The aging Rolling Stones need patching up by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material covering a wound, a medical dressing.

clue.text: City dweller on a panel is confused about Italian

indicators.note: the confused letters go about, around, the Italian letters
confused letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A townsman serving on a committee is bewildered by the Italian language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is confused' makes NEAPOLAN from ON A PANEL; 'about' puts it round IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is someone from Naples, a city in southern Italy.

clue.text: Sort of sense unusual deal about a new coastal walk

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a supposed sixth sense

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about, around, the next two
unusual means the letters of deal are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Some odd sixth sense about a fresh deal on a seaside path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns DEAL into LADE; 'about' puts it round AN to give LANADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open promenade, typically along a seafront.

clue.text: Psychological test for Scrabble club?

definitions.meaning: a test in which a subject says the first thing that comes to mind on hearing a prompt
humorously, a society, an association, of people who play with words

explanation.definitionFit: Psychologists use free word association tests, and a Scrabble society is jokingly an association of word players.

clue.text: Bankrupted daughter in surfing accident

indicators.note: the daughter letter goes in the surfing word

parts.note: a wipeout is a fall from a surfboard
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl is ruined after a fall from her surfboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wiped out financially has lost everything, which is being bankrupted.

clue.text: Where batsman needs to be to make gains

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman must be inside the crease, the line marked at the batting end, to avoid being run out

explanation.walkthrough: The crease in cricket is the line a batsman must be behind, in his ground, to be safe from run-outs.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to grow larger, to make gains, and a safe batsman is in the crease.

clue.text: Each year, or as planned, left to get protection from the sun

parts.note: pa is per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: planned letters are arranged to a design, so or as is rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to take time off each year, as arranged, to stay out of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella used to shade oneself from the sun.

clue.text: Government prescribed diet, for the most part

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a regimen is a prescribed course of diet or exercise

explanation.surface: Officials prescribe a diet for most of the population.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a government, especially an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Love to make a permanent mark, getting award

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a scar is a lasting mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: Romance leaves a lasting mark, and earns a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is an Academy Award, the best-known film prize.

clue.text: Take turns hill-climbing before cooking tea

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the hill letters reverse

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: cooking stirs ingredients together, so the letters of tea are mixed

explanation.surface: Walkers take turns climbing a hill before brewing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns TOR into ROT; 'cooking' turns TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to take turns in sequence, as players rotate positions.

clue.text: Without a hope, crosses state

indicators.note: the answer crosses the word boundaries, sitting inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone hopeless crosses the border in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Acts to recruit good magistrates

indicators.note: recruiting takes someone in, so the acts word contains the good letter

parts.note: does means acts or performs

explanation.surface: Laws are passed to enlist good judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Doges were the chief magistrates of the old republics of Venice and Genoa.

clue.text: Rescue silver stolen from barbarian

indicators.note: something stolen is removed, so the silver letters come out

parts.note: a savage is an uncivilised person, a barbarian
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A plea to recover silverware taken by a marauder.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone is to rescue them from harm.

clue.text: Other men turn it into food

indicators.note: other means the letters take a different order

explanation.surface: A different group of men converts something into a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, food that sustains the body.

clue.text: Not swayed by a French proposal to start disarming

parts.note: un is the French for a
a move is a proposal or suggestion

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of disarming

explanation.surface: A French plan to begin disarmament is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmoved is not swayed by emotion or argument.

clue.text: Phones boss, determined

parts.note: the head is the boss or chief
set means determined or resolved

explanation.surface: A resolute boss makes a telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of headphones, informally phones.
